BiblicalUsage: Agol means circular or round — and it appears only in the description of the temple's great bronze sea: 'a molten sea, ten cubits from the one brim to the other: it was round all about.' The word belongs to the craftsmen's measurements, to a basin so wide a man could not reach across it, standing on twelve oxen in the temple court. A round thing, named once, in the middle of the house of God.
TheologicalSignificance: A round sea of bronze, ten cubits across — this word only says it was circular, and the measurement is the whole of it.
